newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford Foods sees improvement in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Waterford Foods sees improvement in 1997.

text.p: Waterford Foods Plc said in a results statement on Friday that it expected an improved performance in 1997 due to the implementation of a number of initiatives including cost control measures.
Waterford, who announced earlier that it had received a bid approach from competitor Avonmore Foods Plc, reported a drop of 20 percent in 1996 pre-tax profit to 19.8 million Irish pounds.

"The rebalancing of milk costs and market returns and other initiatives such as product development and cost control across the group will improve performance in 1997," managing director Matt Walsh said in a results statement.

Walsh said Waterford Foods entered into 1996 with considerable optimism but a combination of high relative milk prices and market developments created unprecedented pressures and challenges for the group.
He said in spite of corrective actions and positive development in other parts of the group the 1996 results were clearly unsatisfactory.
"A substantial restoration of milk price balance for 1997 has been achieved in Ireland and milk prices continue to moderate in Great Britain and Northern Ireland," Waterford said.
It said market prices remain competitive as a result of continuing GATT obligations and the strength of sterling.
"Nonetheless the prospects for margin recovery in 1997 are encouraging," it said.
Waterford said operating cash flow for 1996 amounted to 44.2 million Irish pounds and net bank borrowings amounted to 215 million which represents a gearing level of 102 percent.

Waterford, who announced a profit warning on March 18, said in Friday's statement that it completed a 35 million sterling private placement with institutional investors in March which falls due in 2006.
It said it had successfully completed a review of certain of its bank facilities following breaches in some covenants arising from a 1996 pre-tax profit result below anticipated levels.
